# claude-bus — System Map

`claude-bus` is a single C++23 binary (`bus`) plus a per-session **broker daemon** that coordinates many `claude` TUIs running in zellij panes. One human, many agents, one terminal. The broker is the durable, out-of-context system-of-record; everything else reads from or writes through it.

## The seven areas

| Area | What it is |
|---|---|
| **kernel** | Durable storage + wire encoding: append-only byte-offset topic logs, cursors/lastId, the topic registry, hand-rolled JSON, the typed `events.jsonl` parse. The substrate everything sits on. |
| **readers** | Pure, broker-free, cache-free derivations: `(events.jsonl + injected snapshot) -> view`. agent_status (the orthogonal axes), task_model (3-store join), trigger_feed (P3 watchdog), tail_reader/pane_state primitives. |
| **policy** | Per-tick "observe read-only snapshot -> decide -> guard -> emit declarative actions" engine. The broker's autonomous-behavior extension point, kernel-safe by construction (no cursor verb). |
| **delivery** | The `Loop` reactor body — the per-tick push/ack/retry/escalate state machine plus folded watchers. Implements the kernel triad. ~1830 LOC. |
| **broker** | The daemon shell: singleton/lifetime, orphan reap, boot-epoch + surgical wipe, the JSON-RPC handlers, and the wiring that ties the RPC reactor to the delivery Loop. |
| **rpc** | The wire layer + the intake/processing thread split (Pillar-D), the timerfd-driven self-clocking tick, and `dispatch.cpp` — the synchronous TTY-write leaf the tick calls. |
| **pane** | The entire interface to a live `claude` TUI: ANSI screen-scrape reads (`PaneState`) + draft-preserving writes; `tty_policy` decides push-vs-pull. |
| **cli** | The `bus` verb dispatch: flat registry + ~40 handlers; RPC verbs vs direct-$STATE verbs; the byte-parity and exit-code contracts. |

## The library DAG (CMake archives — link boundaries ARE the architecture)

```
            bus_core   (kernel: topic_log, topic_registry, json_min, event,
               |         + state_paths/retention/signals pure helpers)
               |
        +------+------------------+
        |                         |
   bus_readers              bus_pane
   (agent_status,           (pane.cpp/.h, tty_policy:
    task_model,              screen-scrape + safe write;
    trigger_feed,            can ACQUIRE a pane)
    tail_reader,                  |
    pane_state VALUE)             |
        |                         |
   bus_policy                     |
   (policy, recovery,             |
    recovery_actor,               |
    dispatch_actor,               |
    blackboard_actor)             |
        |                         |
        +-----------+-------------+
                    |
              the `bus` binary
        (broker.cpp, delivery.cpp, rpc.cpp,
         dispatch.cpp, bus_main + sub/*)
```

The link boundaries are **load-bearing guards, not bookkeeping**:
- `bus_readers` links `bus_core` ONLY. A reader that reaches for `pane.h`/`paneState()` or the socket fails to LINK. `pane_state.h` (a VALUE struct, split out of `pane.h`) lets readers consume a pane snapshot without being able to *acquire* one — a stray acquisition is a compile error.
- `bus_policy` links `bus_readers`+`bus_core` ONLY. A policy actor literally cannot link the pane cache or the socket — so the worst a runaway actor can do is emit an auditable record. Kernel-safety by build graph, not by review.

## Data flow (the steady-state tick)

```
producers --bus msg enqueue (RPC)--> broker (SOLE writer)
                                        |
                                        v
                              kernel: append-only topic log
                              (byte-offset records, v4 wire format)
                                        |
hooks --append--> events.jsonl         |
        |                               |
        v                               v
   readers: foldTurnState/computeAxes   delivery Loop::tick (one thread)
   -> AgentSnapshot                     - updateContinuity (clock-jump)
        |                               - scanEvents -> onAck (SOLE cursor advance)
        v                               - scanRetries (ack-deadline / re-dispatch)
   policy: PolicyEngine fan-out         - runPolicy (drive actors) <--+
   -> declarative PolicyActions --------+  (engine emits, loop executes)
                                        - dispatch pass over inboxes:
                                            off-TTY -> doorbell, drain pulls
                                            TTY (comms) -> sendToPaneSafe push
                                        - maybeEscalateStuck / trim / token-scan
                                        |
                                        v
                              pane: ANSI read gate + draft-preserving write
                                        |
                                        v
                              the agent's claude TUI (fresh user turn)
```

Off-TTY (fleet default): the broker does NOT push; the agent's drain hook PULLS queued mail as `additionalContext` and emits a `bus-ack` event by msg_id. An idle off-TTY agent is woken by the `[bus-wake]` doorbell. The lone TTY agent (`comms`, the human's attached pane) gets pushed via `sendToPaneSafe` under a per-pane flock.

## The kernel triad (the irreducible correctness core)

Three primitives the whole system rests on (docs/broker-spec.md §kernel, broker-seam-redesign §1):

1. **Append-only byte-offset log.** Offsets are stable forever once written; a cursor is just a `u64` file position. `append()` is all-or-nothing (EINTR-loop + ftruncate rollback on torn write); `parseFrom` refuses a torn tail.
2. **Cursor advances ONLY on ack.** An un-acked record sits at the head and is re-evaluated next tick — so **retry is free, not machinery**. The sole advance path is `Loop::onAck -> advanceCursorMonotonic`, whose never-rewind one-liner is what stops a duplicate/out-of-order ack from re-delivering.
3. **Boot-epoch stamp.** Fences pre-boot records so a reboot of a now-durable ($STATE under XDG) log can't re-deliver yesterday's mail as new.

**Tension baked into the triad:** the epoch is the "third primitive" but it lives OUTSIDE the kernel files — it is stamped into the low 8 bytes of the 16-byte `correlation` field (nominally "RPC pairing") by `delivery::stampEpoch`. A redesign touching the wire format must decide: promote epoch to a first-class field (v4->v5 + migration) or keep the overload. Single-writer atomicity (no locks anywhere) is likewise an unenforced *assumption* the whole broker leans on, not an enforced invariant.

# Per-Area Briefs

Each brief: **what** it is, **why** it took this shape, **why it's valuable** (what regresses if removed), and the **live tensions** to discuss at the gate. These surface decisions; they do not prescribe them.

---

## kernel — the durable substrate
**Files:** `topic_log.{cpp,h}`, `topic_registry.{cpp,h}`, `json_min.{cpp,h}`, `event.{cpp,h}` (the `bus_core` archive).

**What.** The append-only, byte-offset-addressed per-topic log (v4 wire format) with the cursor/lastId primitives; the declarative topic registry persisted to `topics.json`; the broker's hand-rolled JSON (no floats, 256-depth cap); and the single typed parse of one `events.jsonl` line.

**Why this shape.** One bet drives everything: a durable, out-of-context broker beats in-context coordination. Persistence forces every choice below it. Byte-offsets (not indices) are stable forever, which is what makes "cursor advances only on ack" free. Single-writer is the load-bearing simplifying assumption — the broker is the only appender on one thread, so `append()` needs no flock/atomicity and can fstat-write-ftruncate-rollback safely. The torn-record rollback exists because a short write under O_APPEND misframes the *entire* tail silently. json_min is hand-rolled for zero deps in a reproducible Nix env. `event.h` parses-once-into-a-typed-struct to kill N divergent ad-hoc scanners.

**Why valuable.** Each piece guards a specific guarantee: drop the torn-write rollback and one short write silently corrupts the whole log tail (the hardest bug to find — silent and delayed); drop `advanceCursorMonotonic`'s never-rewind and a duplicate ack re-delivers; remove the json_min depth cap and a one-packet `[[[...` SIGSEGVs the broker (a real CRIT finding); remove `getOrAutoCreate`'s nested-prefix guard and `inbox-human` silently mints `inbox-inbox-human` (gap #11, already swept once).

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **Epoch is not in the substrate (doc/code divergence).** Docs name boot-epoch as a kernel primitive, but `topic_log` has no epoch concept — it's bolted on by overloading the `correlation` field. The kernel's "third primitive" lives outside the kernel.
- **`max_record_bytes` is dead/absent (doc/code divergence).** Spec says the registry declares it and nothing enforces it; the code carries no such field. Doc overstates what the registry holds — flag which is stale.
- **Single-writer is an unenforced comment.** `append()`'s lock-free correctness is safe ONLY because one thread appends. The exit ramp (tmp+rename or flock) is named, not built.
- `parsed_config` (variant) duplicates `kind_config` (json::Value), kept in sync by hand. `parseIso8601Ms` returns 0 on both "1970" and "parse failed" — indistinguishable downstream. trimHead returns bytes-dropped so the *caller* rebases cursors (offset math leaks into delivery.cpp).

## readers — ground truth to trustworthy view
**Files:** `agent_status.{cpp,h}`, `task_model.{cpp,h}`, `trigger_feed.{cpp,h}`, `pane_state.h`, `tail_reader.h` (the `bus_readers` archive).

**What.** Four pure `(events.jsonl + injected snapshot) -> value` derivations. agent_status folds the whole event sequence into four ORTHOGONAL axes (Process/Turn/Mail/Tui) plus a lossy `State` shim and the doorbell readiness predicate. task_model JOINS three stores (the `tasks` log + `done/` + `triggers/`) into one read model with no new store. trigger_feed crosses URGENCY×SAFETY into an ACT/WAIT/OK signal. pane_state.h and tail_reader.h are the shared primitives.

**Why this shape.** Three pressures: (1) ONE derivation, MANY surfaces — the monitor, agent-bar, state RPC, doorbell, `bus tasks`, critical-path, and triggers must never disagree about an agent. (2) The no-authority invariant, enforced STRUCTURALLY: `pane_state.h` split means a reader can't *name* `paneState()`; the `bus_readers` archive links `bus_core` only, so reaching for the pane or a shared mutable field fails to BUILD. (3) The display must not LIE, and the cheap signal is the wrong one — orthogonal axes preserve per-dimension uncertainty a single enum would force into a lie; `foldTurnState` splits real STUCK (tool overdue) from QUIET (silent, nothing in flight); the continuity clamp stops reboot wall-clock leaps from painting the fleet red.

**Why valuable.** This is the single point where noisy, append-only, clock-sensitive ground truth becomes a trustworthy view — and the trust is enforced by the build graph, not discipline. Collapse the axes and the monitor lies whenever two dimensions disagree (and `wakeReadyForMail` reads axes directly, so a wrong derivation drops real deliveries). Fold pane acquisition in and you break the no-authority invariant on day one and lose unit-testability.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **Namespace proposed, link-boundary built (doc/code divergence).** The seam doc proposed a `bus::readers` namespace; the code stayed flat `bus::` and realized the seam as the CMake archive instead — arguably stronger, but know the doc's plan never landed.
- **`verify` is NOT in the archive.** The doc lists it as a reader; in code it's a CLI-bound one-shot. The seam is concretely THREE TUs, not four.
- **`State` is an explicit compatibility shim** the header tells new callers to avoid — but it's still the wire/render currency of several surfaces; the lossy collapse encodes policy that would have to move.
- `readAgents()` re-folds the ENTIRE event log every call and does NOT use the extracted `TailReader` (which the broker's own three inline copies also don't use yet). `Orchestrating` is mail-receptive but P3-UNSAFE — same label, opposite meaning across two readers, intentional. task_model's `in_flight` is inferred from owner-liveness, not "provably on THIS task." `kStaleBudgetMs` duplicates the broker's env budget and can silently disagree.

## policy — the autonomous-behavior seam
**Files:** `policy.{cpp,h}`, `recovery.{cpp,h}`, `recovery_actor.{cpp,h}`, `dispatch_actor.{cpp,h}`, `blackboard_actor.{cpp,h}` (the `bus_policy` archive); loop side in `delivery.cpp` runPolicy/executePolicyAction.

**What.** A per-tick engine: actors observe a read-only `PolicyContext` snapshot and emit declarative `PolicyAction`s (Enqueue/Recover/Nudge); the engine fans out in registration order and concatenates — no arbitration. recovery.{cpp,h} is the pure, unit-testable breaker/backoff kernel; recovery_actor wraps it. dispatch_actor (1->1 work-queue claim) and blackboard_actor (1->N fan-out) prove the substrate generalizes.

**Why this shape.** One constraint dominates: autonomous behaviors must NOT corrupt the kernel triad. So (1) god-object avoidance — every behavior used to be a method bolted on the 74KB Loop; the seam makes them register against a fixed interface. (2) Kernel-safety by construction — the action vocabulary has NO cursor/ack/write verb, AND `bus_policy` links readers+core only so an actor that reaches for the socket fails to LINK. (3) No engine arbitration — conflicts resolve at EXECUTION via each topic's existing in-flight/breaker/cooldown gating, which only works because every action is idempotent-or-cheaply-redundant. The competing-consumer claim (a claim IS a cursor advance, which actors are forbidden) resolved by putting the advance in the LOOP executor on the actor's declarative `consume_from` intent.

**Why valuable.** It's the one seam that ADDS capability. Without the no-cursor vocabulary + link boundary, every future autonomous behavior again has direct access to delivery state — each new one a fresh "can this corrupt delivery?" audit. It's also the north-star unification: recovery AND the coordination patterns (queue/blackboard/maildir) on ONE engine, one audit trail, one test harness. Inert-by-default (recovery ships in `observe`, dispatch/blackboard inert until their topic exists) is what made it safe to land live.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **Dead breaker path (code/doc divergence).** recovery.cpp implements + unit-tests the full MaxR/MaxT breaker, Relaunch, and `recoveryObserveHealthy` — but the actor only ever calls Clear (R1). The breaker is reachable only from tests today. Is Phase C still coming, or is this premature machinery to trim?
- **No-arbitration is a bet, not a proof.** It holds only because every current action is idempotent. The named revisit-signal: two actors with non-idempotent, conflicting intents on one agent. A future non-idempotent action must add coalescing THEN, not inherit the assumption silently.
- **I/O-ownership asymmetry.** The seam doc says I/O is loop-plane, but RecoveryActor does its OWN ledger file I/O (just not socket/pane). Confirm that's the intended boundary.
- Stale header: dispatch_actor.h still says "one assignment per tick" but the body batch-assigns. `consume_from` is a field on Enqueue, not a Kind. SNAPSHOT growth: queue_head/board_updates are pattern-specific folds the loop does unconditionally every tick.

## delivery — the per-tick reactor
**Files:** `delivery.{cpp,h}` (~1830 LOC), the `Loop` driven from `rpc::Server::run`.

**What.** The single-threaded reactor body. `tick()` runs in order: updateContinuity, scanEvents (->ACK), scanRetries, maybeAutoClear, runPolicy, maybeScanTokens, maybeWakeIdleOffTty (doorbell), maybeTrimLogs, the dispatch pass over every inbox/commands topic, then maybeEscalateStuck. It implements the kernel triad and the two-arm Transport fork (off-TTY pull vs TTY push). Several adjacent watchers (token-scan, escalation, retention, dead-agent prune, suspend/resume clamp) are folded onto the same thread.

**Why this shape.** Three pressures: (1) single-threaded-by-construction safety — the broker is the only writer, so trim/dispatch/ack/retry can't race an append, and putting unrelated watchers here gets serialization for free (there's no second thread to use). (2) Restart-safety — cursor-advances-only-on-ack makes retry free; the boot-epoch fences the durable log against re-delivery. (3) The TTY/off-TTY fork is a DELIBERATE two-case `if`, not a Transport class — the spec calls wrapping it "ceremony over a two-case fork." The dup-delivery scar shapes scanRetries: in-flight⟹already-delivered for TTY, so retry is an ack DEADLINE that escalates after kMaxAttempts and never re-sends, whereas tui-commands genuinely re-dispatch.

**Why valuable.** Each piece maps to a documented scar: drop ack-only cursor advance and retry stops being free; drop the epoch and a reboot re-delivers stale mail (the broker even stamps its own audit emissions or it escalates itself in an infinite loop); collapse the two arms and you either fight the human keyboard or strand every off-TTY agent; drop the doorbell and an idle off-TTY agent sits forever; make scanRetries re-send TTY and the dup-delivery bug returns; drop retention/rebase and the durable logs grow unbounded; drop the live-pane gates and ghost markers fire spurious auto-clears/escalations.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **The Loop is a god-object by another name.** ~1830 LOC of barely-related concerns. The DELIVERY half was shattered into Log/Router/Transport/Readers/Policy, but the watchers (maybeScanTokens/WakeIdleOffTty/AutoClear/EscalateStuck) still live as inline methods, each re-implementing the same readAgents + live-pane-gate + cooldown-map + audit prologue. Which become Policy actors (auto-clear is slated as AutoClearActor) vs stay loop-plane I/O?
- **Epoch lives in a stolen field** (same `correlation` overload as kernel).
- **Positional TTY ack is fragile** — any UserPromptSubmit acks the OLDEST in-flight record; off-TTY fixed this with bus-ack-by-id, TTY (comms only) wasn't. Unify on by-id?
- **Two retry semantics under one name** (ack-deadline vs re-dispatch, keyed off kind + transport arm). The single thread is both the safety guarantee AND the saturation risk (a synchronous pane fork can stall the whole reactor). Retention's clamp has carve-outs (inbox-ops/inbox-human exempted). Continuity detection duplicates recovery's own wall-jump grace.

---

## broker — the daemon shell
**Files:** `broker.cpp` (~1120 lines), `broker.h` (stale skeleton), `signals.h`, `state_paths.h`, `retention.h`.

**What.** The single per-session daemon (`bus broker run`) that owns ALL state and is the only writer to topic logs. Five jobs: singleton + lifetime (flock on broker.pid, orphan reap, PDEATHSIG, boot-epoch bump, surgical wipe of only volatile state); the JSON-RPC handlers; constructing + wiring the delivery Loop into the reactor; three pure supporting headers (signals without SA_RESTART, the single stateRoot() resolver, the table-testable trim math); and the intake/processing thread split that `server.run` hides.

**Why this shape.** Every odd shape is a scar. Single processing thread, zero locks is the load-bearing invariant — one consumer mutates everything so atomicity is free. flock singleton (not O_EXCL+kill) because a rebuild-under-live-process let two brokers run. Orphan reaping because PDEATHSIG is lost when the whole zellij session dies at once — the corpse holds the flock and answers the socket but can't deliver, and a fresh broker would DEFER to it forever (permanent silent outage). Boot-epoch + surgical wipe because $STATE is now durable and would re-deliver yesterday's mail. signals.h drops SA_RESTART so EINTR actually aborts blocking syscalls on SIGTERM.

**Why valuable.** Drop the single-consumer model and every other coordination pattern's race-freedom breaks (there are no locks BECAUSE there's one thread). Drop orphan reaping and a crash/suspend/reboot causes a permanent silent fleet outage. Drop the boot epoch and every restart is a re-delivery bomb. Drop the per-kind retry distinction and the dup-delivery bug returns. Drop the retention clamp and undelivered mail gets trimmed away.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **broker.h is stale (doc/code divergence).** Its comment says "Phase 4b.1 skeleton: only a ping op" but broker.cpp implements ~1000 lines more. A redesigner reading only the .h badly misjudges scope.
- **The broker is mostly NOT in broker.cpp.** The delivery state machine lives in delivery.{cpp,h}. broker.cpp is the lifecycle shell + RPC surface. A "broker redesign" touching only this file misses the engine.
- **The `state` handler forks paneState() per agent on every ~1Hz call** — the exact fan-out cost the intake-decouple doc named; mitigated by the thread split but the cost remains (inotify cache promised, not here).
- DROP handler does an O(all-records) linear scan. GC is explicit-only by design (a booting agent's unregistered inbox must not be reapable). The Transport seam is a documented FORK, not a class — `comms` must NEVER collapse into the off-TTY arm.

---

## rpc — the wire layer + intake/processing split
**Files:** `rpc.{cpp,h}` (the broker wire layer), `dispatch.{cpp,h}` (the TTY-write leaf).

**What.** Line-delimited JSON-RPC over a Unix socket, one request+response per connection. `rpc::call()` is the client; `Server::run()` is the heart — the Pillar-D split: an INTAKE thread only accepts/parses and hands the live conn_fd to a bounded CmdQueue (eventfd signal); a single PROCESSING thread drains the queue, runs each Handler, writes the reply, and drives the tick. Processing owns a timerfd armed to the soonest deadline plus a 250ms base-cadence floor — so the tick fires on three wake sources (queued command, deadline, idle floor). dispatch.cpp is the synchronous TTY-write leaf: flock the per-pane lock, check INSERT-readiness, write via sendToPane, else normalize + back off (0.25/1/4s, ~5.25s worst case), polling stopRequested() every 50ms.

**Why this shape.** The decouple is forced by one problem: the broker was one reactor doing two fighting jobs. Intake and the delivery tick (which forks zellij per agent) shared one thread; under fan-out the tick serialized into tens of seconds and the broker went "down-while-alive" (the live 2026-05-31 outage). The flip side: on a quiet fleet the tick only advanced on incidental RPC traffic, stalling retry/escalation. The split + timerfd fix both. SINGLE processing consumer (not a pool) is dictated by the lock-free atomicity the rest of the broker leans on. dispatch.cpp's stop-flag-polling sleeps exist because a multi-second TTY retry sits directly on the processing thread.

**Why valuable.** Remove the split and the fan-out wedge returns (the exact outage). Remove the timerfd and a viewerless fleet stops escalating/retrying/reclaiming. Remove single-consumer ("just add locks") and you trade by-construction atomicity for hand-maintained locking the broker was built to avoid. Remove the bounded queue and a fast producer blows memory — or, "fixed" by blocking intake, recreates the wedge. Remove the inode-guard in ~Server and a shutting-down broker unlinks a successor's socket. On dispatch: remove the flock and concurrent producers interleave bytes at one TTY; remove the stop-poll backoff and a stuck pane parks the delivery thread past SIGTERM.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **Four doc/code divergences.** Queue depth: doc says 1024, code uses 256 (code is the intended revision — preserve the shallow-queue reasoning, not the number). Reactor primitive: doc says epoll, code uses pselect (behaviorally equal; §8 future-work assumes an epoll set that doesn't exist). Shutdown handshake: doc proposes shutdown(listen_fd), code uses SOCK_NONBLOCK + 250ms poll-recheck (the documented fix for the SIGTERM-wedge — load-bearing, keep it). Intake read deadline: doc anticipated a read deadline, code uses SO_RCVTIMEO/SNDTIMEO 5s (CRIT #2 fix).
- **FD-ownership contract is subtle:** once enqueued, processing owns close() on every path; intake closes only what it never enqueued. Exact-once-close — a redesign must preserve it or risk EMFILE / double-close.
- `rearm()` clamps past-due to 1ms (never 0) — REQUIRES the deadline source to escalate-once or it busy-loops; that correctness lives outside this file (delivery's `_alarmed_` sets). **dispatch.cpp is NOT covered by the decouple doc** — its ~5.25s worst case sits on the processing thread (the named future escape: async pane I/O worker pool). FlockGuard's blocking LOCK_EX has no stop-flag check during acquire.

## pane — the interface to a live claude TUI
**Files:** `pane.{cpp,h}`, `tty_policy.h`.

**What.** The entire channel into a zellij pane running a `claude` TUI. Reads pane state by parsing the ANSI screen dump into a structured `PaneState` (mode / input buffer / ghost suggestion / bypass flag); writes via write-chars + Enter. Five capabilities: `paneId` (resolve title->terminal_N), `sendToPane` (raw, no draft preservation), `sendToPaneSafe` (draft-preserving: refuse on unknown/LOCKED/bypass-off, snapshot draft, clean buffer, write, re-type draft), `sendKey`, and `paneState`/`paneStateCached` (TTL-cached reads). All subprocess work goes through runCapture/runSilent (fork+exec, 5s deadline, SIGKILL on overrun). tty_policy.h is the orthogonal routing decision: which agents get pushed (TTY) vs pulled (off-TTY drain).

**Why this shape.** Three pressures. (1) There is no API into a running claude TUI — the only channel is the terminal's screen + keystrokes, so the whole layer is screen-scraping (ANSI SGR parse to separate the human's draft from claude's dim ghost autocomplete; whole-screen footer scan because tall panes push the footer off any fixed window). (2) Every zellij call runs synchronously on the broker's single delivery thread — so a hung child halts ALL delivery, driving the 5s deadline+SIGKILL and BOTH TTL caches (which collapsed the per-tick fork storm behind the 2026-05-31 fan-out outage). (3) The pane is SHARED with a human who may be typing — so safe writes preserve a draft, defer rather than clobber on unreadable state, and flatten `\n`->space. tty_policy's opt-out lives in COMMITTED config (not $STATE) because a $STATE sentinel kept getting wiped on relaunch and silently reverting the fleet to TTY.

**Why valuable.** Drop ANSI dim-classification and you can't separate human draft from ghost suggestion. Drop the whole-screen footer scan and the bast-wedge returns (alt-status footer -> mode=unknown -> defers forever). Drop the `\n`->space flatten and concurrent typing fragments injected messages. Drop the 5s deadline and one slow dump-screen freezes the whole loop. Drop either TTL cache and the fork storm starves RPC. Drop tty_policy's committed opt-out and `comms` (the human's pane) silently loses immediate delivery when attached-but-idle.

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **The state RPC bypasses the cache (divergence the audit flags).** broker.cpp's state RPC calls RAW `paneState` per agent per ~1Hz poll — NOT `paneStateCached` (which the delivery-loop gates correctly use). Should the state RPC share the loop's cache or keep raw reads for monitor freshness?
- **Wasted work the audit exposes:** the per-poll scan fetches buffer/mode/bypass but the monitor renders NONE of them — real needs reduce to pane_exists + a mode supplement. Candidate cuts: drop unused fields, or feed pane_exists from a lifecycle file so the scan goes away.
- **Screen-scraping is inherently fragile** — every heuristic is coupled to claude-TUI's exact rendering and breaks silently on a restyle. Worth weighing a hook-stamped mode-to-file channel.
- Two TTL knobs with different defaults/semantics (300ms per-name vs ~1-3s global keep-last-good) — intentional asymmetry, sharp if unified. sendToPaneSafe FALLS THROUGH to raw write when dump-screen fails entirely — a transient hiccup can still clobber a draft. Multi-line drafts truncate to the first row. (doc line numbers in pane-read-audit.md have drifted; claims hold.)

## cli — the `bus` verb surface
**Files:** `bus_main.cpp`, `bus.{cpp,h}`, `sub.h`, `sub/sub_*.cpp` (~40 handlers).

**What.** A flat verb->handler registry plus ~40 subcommand handlers. bus_main is a 17-line argv parser; bus.cpp holds the static `kSubcommands[]` array that drives both dispatch and `bus help`. Families: meta, pane primitives (`msg send` flocked safe write vs `pane-send` raw), produce/consume (RPC, except `done`/`task set` which write $STATE directly and `msg drain` the off-TTY hook engine), topic registry, lifecycle (spawn/restore-peers/despawn shell to agent-launch; recover with exit codes 0/10/20/30), broker, and viewers. Two dispatch styles: top-level registry entries vs noun sub-dispatchers (msg/topic/tasks/broker). Arg parsing is hand-rolled per handler; output is human column tables; `--json` exists only on `bus agents`.

**Why this shape.** It's a port of a pile of shell scripts into one C++23 binary, done phase by phase — so a flat function-pointer registry is the minimum mechanism to land one verb per phase (one array row + one decl + one .cpp). Output and exit codes are pinned to byte-for-byte parity with the scripts they replaced because live callers (awk parsers, drain hooks, the broker's delivery path) depend on the exact text — which is why parsing/formatting stayed hand-rolled and local. The RPC-vs-direct-$STATE split traces to the single-writer rule: `done`/`task set` write $STATE directly precisely so the signal survives a broker outage / agent /clear.

**Why valuable.** The registry + uniform signature is what makes `bus` the unified entry point — every capability reachable as `bus <verb>` with `$CLAUDE_BUS_AGENT_ID` ambient (the load-bearing sender convention). Specific irreplaceable pieces: `recover`'s exit-code protocol IS the interface the auto-recovery engine reads; `msg drain`'s bus-ack-on-inject is the cursor-advance gate that makes off-TTY delivery exactly-once; `done`/`verify`'s deliberate broker-independence is the only signal catching the fleet's recurring false-completion failure; `tasks`/`topic`'s unknown-verb-errors (exit 2, never an empty table) encode "the monitor must not lie."

**Tensions for the gate.**
- **docs/bus-commands.md is significantly behind.** Omits ~13 live verbs (done, log, monitor, recover, restore-peers, despawn, roles, tasks, task, triggers, verify, agents, introduce, state-root) and broker info/gc + msg drain/drop. `--title` is now INERT (doc describes retired behavior). "only broker verb" is wrong (run/info/gc). Treat the doc as stale annotation; `bus help` is canonical.
- **No shared flag parser** — every handler re-implements `--flag value` loops; behavior already diverges (some honor `--`, most don't; some reject unknown flags, older ones treat them as positionals). Unifiable, but must preserve per-command byte-exact usage + exit-2.
- **Exit codes are API** (recover 0/10/20/30, verify 1-on-missing) — load-bearing, don't normalize away.
- **RPC-vs-direct-write split is deliberate and asymmetric** — "route everything through the broker for consistency" would destroy verify's independence (the whole P5 point). Stale /tmp paths in sub_inbox/sub_events header comments. Self-path resolution duplicated (sub_lifecycle + sub_roles, hard-coded /home/sulin fallbacks). spawn/restore-peers/despawn have real side effects on the LIVE zellij session — not $STATE-sandboxable.

# Guided Reading Order

A single path that climbs the dependency graph from the durable core outward to the surfaces. Each hop names the one thing it unlocks for the next.

## 0. Orientation (before any code)
- **docs/broker-spec.md §The kernel** — read FIRST. The three primitives (append-log, ack-only cursor, boot-epoch) and the off-TTY-default delivery model are the contract every file below implements.
  *Why: everything else is mechanism around this; without the triad in hand the code reads as arbitrary.*

## 1. kernel — the substrate
- `src/topic_log.h` (the v4 wire-format header comment, lines 1-32) -> `topic_log.cpp` (`append`, then `parseFrom`, then `advanceCursorMonotonic`) -> `json_min.h/.cpp` (the depth-cap comment) -> `topic_registry.{h,cpp}` (`getOrAutoCreate`) -> `event.{h,cpp}` (`parseEvent`).
  *Why this first: it owns durability and the byte-offset addressing the cursor rests on. The single-writer assumption stated in topic_log.h licenses every lock-free choice above it — internalize it before you see code that depends on it.*

## 2. readers — ground truth -> view
- `src/pane_state.h` (the injected VALUE type + the header-graph boundary) -> `tail_reader.h` -> `agent_status.h` (events/fold/axes/continuity-clamp) -> `agent_status.cpp` (`foldTurnState`, then `computeAxes` with the STUCK-vs-QUIET split, then `computeState`/`wakeReadyForMail`) -> `trigger_feed.{h,cpp}` -> `task_model.{h,cpp}`.
  *Why next: readers turn the kernel's `events.jsonl` into the orthogonal-axis snapshot that policy observes and the doorbell gates on. You must understand what an AgentSnapshot MEANS before reading who consumes it.*

## 3. policy — the safe extension point
- `src/policy.h` (the kernel-guard thesis + the full contract) -> `policy.cpp` (trivial fan-out) -> `recovery.{h,cpp}` (the pure breaker/backoff kernel) -> `recovery_actor.{h,cpp}` (the proving actor, R1-R4) -> `dispatch_actor` / `blackboard_actor` (the 1->1 and 1->N shapes).
  *Why here: policy depends ONLY on readers+core, so it slots in before the loop that drives it. Reading it now shows what the loop's runPolicy must NOT let actors do — the no-cursor-verb vocabulary frames the delivery code that follows.*

## 4. delivery — the reactor that ties it together
- `docs/broker-spec.md §Delivery + §Reliability + §Retention` -> `src/delivery.h` (the in-flight/ack/epoch contract) -> `delivery.cpp` top->`tick()` (the ordered list), then `dispatchAgentInbox` (the gate ladder), then `scanEvents`/`onAck` (the SOLE cursor advance) -> finally `runPolicy`/`executePolicyAction` and the folded watchers.
  *Why now: delivery consumes all three prior layers — it appends to kernel logs, reads reader snapshots, and drives policy actors. tick() is the one screen where the whole steady state is visible.*

## 5. broker / rpc — the daemon that hosts the loop
- `src/state_paths.h` (40 lines: why $STATE is durable now) -> `broker.cpp` lines 1-352 (the lifecycle prologue: flock, orphan reap, PDEATHSIG, epoch bump, surgical wipe) -> the RPC handler registrations (enqueue + drain are the produce/consume halves) -> the one line `server.run(250ms, dl.tick, ...)` -> `docs/broker-intake-decouple.md §1-§6` -> `rpc.h` (the Server::run comment) -> `rpc.cpp` (CmdQueue + knobs, then `bind`, then `run`'s process_main + intake loop) -> `signals.h`.
  *Why after delivery: broker.cpp is the shell that CONSTRUCTS and wires the loop you just read; rpc.cpp is the threading that drives it. Reading the engine first makes "what server.run hides" concrete instead of abstract.*

## 6. pane — the synchronous leaf the tick calls
- `src/tty_policy.h` (push-vs-pull: WHY a write happens) -> `pane.h` (the whole header — the comments ARE the design spec) -> `pane.cpp` (subprocess plumbing -> ANSI/parse helpers -> `sendToPaneSafe`, then `paneState`) -> `src/dispatch.cpp` (`dispatchTui`: flock -> isReady -> backoff) -> `docs/pane-read-audit.md` (the cross-area consumer map, read last).
  *Why here: pane is the bottom of the write path. Every per-tick fork the delivery loop and the broker's state RPC make lands here — its 5s deadline + TTL caches are the reason the single thread doesn't wedge. You now have the callers in hand to see why each gate exists.*

## 7. cli — the human/agent surface
- `src/bus_main.cpp` (the 17-line dispatcher) -> `bus.cpp` (the `kSubcommands[]` registry — the canonical verb list) -> `bus.h` + `sub.h` -> `sub/sub_meta.cpp` -> `sub/sub_pane.cpp` (the flock-vs-raw split + byte-parity) -> `sub/sub_msg.cpp` + `sub_produce.cpp` + `sub_consume.cpp` (the RPC-vs-$STATE split + the drain off-TTY engine) -> `sub_tasks.cpp` (the richest sub-dispatcher, unknown-verb discipline) -> `sub_lifecycle.cpp` (recover's exit-code protocol) -> `sub_verify.cpp`.
  *Why last: the CLI is the thinnest layer — every verb is a thin reader of, or producer into, the machinery you've now read top to bottom. It reads fastest once the broker/kernel contracts are familiar, and its byte-parity + exit-code contracts only make sense knowing who consumes them.*
